answer: The walnut multiplier is published, charged in copper, and sonnet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1705 identities would post 4013 proofs and burn roughly 66 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
